# getByteSize

<link-summary>Returns the length of a string in code units.</link-summary>

<web-summary>getByteSize() — Returns the length of a string in code units. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function getByteSize(value: string): number;
```

**Read the caveat before using this.** The name and the original intent are the UTF-8 byte length, but as it stands the function counts UTF-16 code units and only widens the first surrogate it meets. An ASCII string measures correctly; anything outside ASCII — Cyrillic, Greek, CJK, an emoji — measures short. Until that is fixed, measure a payload with `Utilities.newBlob(text).getBytes().length` instead.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description            |
| :-------- | :------- | :--------------------- |
| `value`   | `string` | The string to measure. |

## Returns

`number` — the length, in code units.

## Throws

| Exception                | Condition                  |
| :----------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `InvalidStringException` | the value is not a string. |

## Examples

### In use

```javascript
getByteSize("abc"); // => 3
```
